D14·jrys — 2026-09-22
chose: 2.4 CONTRACT (native-memory import, under D13).
(a) SURFACE: `sofar remember --from-native [--dir <path>] [--initiative <slug>]`. It is operator-only and runs only on a terminal (stdin and stderr are TTYs, not CI), as `sofar check --approve` does. From an agent shell it appends nothing and reports how many entries are waiting. No MCP tool, no hook, no automatic run.
(b) SOURCE: Claude Code auto memory. The directory is taken from, in order:
- --dir;
- autoMemoryDirectory in .claude/settings.local.json or ~/.claude/settings.json, with ~ expanded (never the checked-in .claude/settings.json, which Claude ignores for this key);
- ~/.claude/projects/<the main worktree's path, every non-alphanumeric character as '-'>/memory/.
Only topic files directly in it count: MEMORY.md and subdirectories such as team/ are out. An entry's type is frontmatter `type` or `metadata.type`. Only project and reference entries are offered; user, feedback and untyped entries are counted and never shown. Codex memories are out: they carry no type, so D13 cannot admit them.
(c) REVIEW: each candidate shows its file, type, name, description and full body. Lines that look like secrets are flagged: key or token assignments, passwords, private-key blocks, known token prefixes. Answers:
- y imports it;
- n declines it, remembered on this clone and not offered again until the file changes;
- s or Enter skips it for now;
- q stops.
(d) WRITE: an approved entry appends memory_promoted {text: description then body, origin: "claude-memory:<file>@<first 16 hex of the file's sha256>"}, with actor human and source cli. The new optional `origin` field, valid only on memory_promoted, marks the words as native memory's. An entry already imported with the same digest is not offered again. One whose file changed since its import is offered as an update that supersedes the earlier import, stamped per D12.
(e) RENDER: the digest's memory section and memory.md mark a memory that carries an origin with `(from Claude memory, not the operator's words)`.
(f) DECLINES live in the per-clone state dir (<state>/native-memory/<clone key>.json), never in the record: a decline is private.
(g) sofar commits nothing; the operator commits. No model call. rust-core mirrors the origin field (fingerprint) and the render mark as 2.10.
over: An MCP tool (an agent could run the import). A SessionStart nudge counting pending entries (an automatic surface the ruling keeps off). Importing Codex memory without a type (the ruling admits only typed project and reference entries). A new event type for imports (memory_promoted already is the repo-memory fact; a new type needs its own drift class and rust mirror). Recording declines in the record (a decline would publish that the entry exists).
because: D13 fixes the policy, and this is the smallest surface that honours every clause of it. The terminal gate is the one `sofar check --approve` already uses to stop an agent approving its own act. Carrying the origin in the payload, not the text, keeps it machine-checkable: the benchmark can assert that no sofar-arm memory carries one (MOAT.md P2).
